lead.text: *Not one-line prompts. Complete workflows — with human checkpoints.*
A prompt is a single request. A workflow is a sequence of prompts with human review between them. Workflows are how AI stops being a novelty and becomes a genuine productivity multiplier.

Each workflow below is described as a sequence of steps: what AI does, what YOU verify, and how the two handoffs combine. These are the ones worth investing in — the ones that repay their setup time many times over.

blocks.text: A Sunday-night workflow that produces genuine planning, not to-do padding.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Dump raw notes from your week into a doc: what you did, what surprised you, what went badly, what went well.
2. [AI] Ask AI to identify 3 themes emerging from the raw notes and 2 things you seem to be avoiding.
3. [YOU] Sit with the reflection. Is AI right about the themes? Right about the avoidance?
4. [YOU] Write next week's Top Three, informed by the reflection.
5. [AI] Ask AI to check whether the Top Three actually address the themes, or if they are a repeat of last week's pattern.
6. [YOU] Adjust. Book them into your calendar.
WATCH OUT FOR

• AI will tell you what you want to hear if you frame the input to invite it. Include the ugly parts.
• Don't outsource the sitting-with. AI's reflection is no substitute for yours.
For days with 5+ meetings, an AI-assisted flow that prevents you from arriving unprepared or leaving without clear next steps.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] The night before, list every meeting with 3 fields each: attendees, stated goal, what YOU need out of it.
2. [AI] Ask AI to generate a 5-minute prep for each meeting: two questions to be ready to answer, two questions to ask, the outcome to push for.
3. [YOU] Skim the preps in the morning. Add anything AI missed.
4. [YOU] Take real notes during each meeting.
5. [AI] After the day, feed the notes to AI and ask for a summary organized by: decisions made, action items with owner/date, unresolved issues.
6. [YOU] Verify AI's summary against your memory. Send the cleaned summary to attendees.
WATCH OUT FOR

• AI will invent action items it thinks 'should' have been assigned. Verify each one existed.
• Do not use AI as a replacement for taking notes. Real notes hold what AI can only guess at.

entries.title: Workflow 3: Deep-Dive Research on an Unfamiliar Topic

blocks.text: The 90-minute AI-augmented version of Level 3's research protocol.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Write the specific question you're trying to answer, in one sentence.
2. [AI] Ask AI for a plain-language explanation of the topic, the 5 core concepts, the 3 most authoritative sources to read, and the 2 most common misconceptions.
3. [YOU] Actually read one of the recommended sources. AI's summary is a scaffold, not a substitute.
4. [AI] After the reading, ask AI to synthesize what you now know with what it originally said. What did the primary source change?
5. [YOU] Draft a 2-paragraph summary in your own words.
6. [AI] Have AI critique your summary. Where is it vague? Where might it be wrong?
7. [YOU] Revise. Publish or file for future reference.
WATCH OUT FOR

• AI-generated 'authoritative sources' are frequently hallucinated. Verify each source actually exists.
• Do not stop at AI's plain-language explanation. That is the beginning, not the end.
For high-stakes emails, letters, or documents that will be read multiple times.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Draft the message yourself first — including the parts that feel awkward. Do not use AI as a starting point.
2. [AI] Ask AI to critique your draft: where is it unclear, where is it likely to be misread, where is the tone off?
3. [YOU] Revise, keeping YOUR voice.
4. [AI] Ask AI to predict the two most likely responses from the recipient — one favorable, one unfavorable.
5. [YOU] Adjust the message to preempt the unfavorable response if possible.
6. [AI] One final check: read this back to me as if I were the recipient. What does it feel like?
7. [YOU] Send when you're ready. Do not send after 9 pm.
WATCH OUT FOR

• Do not let AI write the message from scratch. Your voice will disappear. The recipient will notice.
• AI's 'this is how it feels' output can be overly reassuring. Trust your own re-read too.

entries.title: Workflow 5: Structured Learning of a New Skill

blocks.text: The AI-augmented version of the 90-minute skill sprint.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Define what 'operational' means for this skill — what specific ability do you need?
2. [AI] Ask for a 90-minute learning plan: 30 minutes understand, 45 minutes practice, 15 minutes teach.
3. [YOU] Do the 30 minutes of understanding — reading and note-taking.
4. [AI] Ask AI to quiz you on the concepts. Answer, get corrections, drill on the gaps.
5. [YOU] Do the 45 minutes of hands-on practice. Break things. Rebuild.
6. [AI] When stuck, ask AI as a tutor — not as an answer-key. 'Why is this happening?' not 'give me the fix.'
7. [YOU] Do the 15 minutes of explaining out loud to an imaginary beginner. Where you stumble, drill.
8. [YOU] Stop. Come back only when a specific real situation demands it.
WATCH OUT FOR

• AI is a tutor, not a substitute for practice. Reading AI's explanations is not learning.
• The 'teach it back' step is essential. Don't skip it because AI already 'covered' the material.
One of the highest-ROI uses of an AI tool in a professional life.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Gather: the offer, your target, your BATNA, market data, your leverage story.
2. [AI] Ask for the strongest case for your target number, the three most likely pushbacks, and the specific opening sentence.
3. [YOU] Rehearse the opening sentence out loud until it's natural.
4. [AI] Role-play as the hiring manager. Push back realistically. Practice your counter-responses.
5. [YOU] Note the pushbacks that surprised you. Prepare answers.
6. [AI] Second round: role-play a HARDER hiring manager. Do not go easy.
7. [YOU] Also decide, in advance, your walkaway number — the point at which you decline.
8. [YOU] Have the actual negotiation. Silence after your ask. Don't negotiate against yourself.
WATCH OUT FOR

• AI can be overly confident about market ranges. Cross-check with 2+ live sources.
• Rehearsing does not eliminate the need to sleep the night before.
The Level 5 process-improvement workflow, augmented.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Shadow the process — watch someone actually do it. Take notes.
2. [YOU] Draw the actual current-state process map.
3. [AI] Feed AI the process description. Ask: where are the likely error points, waste steps, automation candidates?
4. [YOU] Verify AI's suggestions against reality. Some will be wrong; some will be spot on.
5. [AI] Ask for the ONE change with highest leverage, with the specific risk of that change.
6. [YOU] Propose the change. Run it for 4 weeks. Measure.
7. [AI] After 4 weeks, feed AI the results. Ask for second-order effects to watch for.
8. [YOU] Adapt. Scale or revert. Write up honestly.
WATCH OUT FOR
• AI will suggest changes that ignore political / regulatory / relational constraints. Filter its suggestions through domain reality.
For contracts, reports, papers, or dense documentation.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] State the specific question you're trying to answer with this document.
2. [AI] Feed AI the document with the question. Ask for: (1) the answer, (2) the 5 quotes from the document that support the answer, (3) anything in the document that would contradict the answer.
3. [YOU] Verify the 5 quotes actually appear in the document.
4. [AI] Ask AI what it thinks it might have missed or misunderstood.
5. [YOU] For any consequential decision, read the specific sections yourself before acting.
WATCH OUT FOR

• AI hallucinates specific quotes from long documents. Every quote must be verifiable.
• For legal, medical, or financial documents, AI is a starting point. A qualified professional is the final word.

entries.title: Workflow 9: Weekly Personal Report to Your Manager

blocks.text: A 15-minute Friday habit that dramatically improves your manager-relationship over months.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] List everything you did this week — even the small things. Bullet points.
2. [AI] Ask AI to organize into: what shipped, what's in progress, what's blocked, what needs input, what went sideways.
3. [YOU] Review. AI often omits or over-inflates. Fix.
4. [AI] Ask AI to draft a 5-bullet Friday email in your voice.
5. [YOU] Edit until it sounds like YOU wrote it. Send.
6. [YOU] File the bullets — you'll want them for your next review or promotion case.
WATCH OUT FOR
• AI writes in a generic corporate voice. Rewrite in yours or your manager will read it as autopilot.
For the type of decision that shapes years — a job, a role, a move.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Write out the decision, your current situation, your goals, your constraints.
2. [AI] Ask AI to walk you through the Decision 7 framework, asking the sharpest question at each step.
3. [YOU] Answer honestly. Do not smooth the answers.
4. [AI] Have AI generate a pre-mortem for each option — how each choice could fail in a year.
5. [YOU] Talk to at least 2 humans who have made similar moves. AI cannot substitute.
6. [AI] Feed the human conversations back to AI. Ask: what did I learn from those humans that AI missed?
7. [YOU] Sleep on it. Then decide with confidence. Journal the reasoning.
WATCH OUT FOR

• AI has no stake in your outcome — which is a strength for objectivity, and a weakness for judgment about your specific life.
• Humans who have done the thing know things AI doesn't. Do not skip them.
After a project — success or failure — the workflow that turns experience into learning.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Write a raw timeline: what happened, when, who did what. Do not editorialize.
2. [AI] Feed AI the timeline. Ask: what decisions do you see, and at each decision, what was the fork?
3. [AI] Ask AI to identify the top 3 decisions that most affected the outcome — for better or worse.
4. [YOU] For each of those decisions, ask: was it reasonable given what we knew? Or did we know something we ignored?
5. [AI] Ask AI what the equivalent situation next time would look like — what specific pattern should we watch for?
6. [YOU] Write the actual post-mortem. What we did, what we learned, what we're changing. Share it widely.
WATCH OUT FOR
• AI is prone to results-based thinking: 'the decision was bad because the outcome was bad.' Push back explicitly.
For projects requiring buy-in from multiple parties with different concerns.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] List each stakeholder, their role, their likely interests, and what you've already tried.
2. [AI] Ask AI to identify what each stakeholder is likely to be worried about that they haven't said.
3. [AI] Ask AI to draft a talking-point kit for each stakeholder — same core message, adapted to each person's concerns.
4. [YOU] Have the individual conversations. LISTEN. Adjust your model of each person's concerns based on what they actually say.
5. [AI] Feed AI what you learned. Ask: given the new information, who is the most important next conversation to have, and what should I say differently?
6. [YOU] Iterate. Real alignment is built one conversation at a time.
WATCH OUT FOR
• AI-generated 'likely concerns' are educated guesses. Do not treat them as facts about specific humans.
An annual workflow to keep your compensation conversation informed.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Update your CV with the last 12 months' impact — quarterly, so this isn't a scramble.
2. [AI] Ask AI to identify the achievements most likely to matter for level advancement in your field.
3. [YOU] Research current market ranges via 2+ live sources.
4. [AI] Given your role and market, ask AI to build the strongest case for a raise / promotion.
5. [YOU] Refine into your own voice. Book the conversation.
6. [AI] Role-play the pushbacks you might get.
7. [YOU] Have the actual conversation. Silence after your ask.
WATCH OUT FOR
• AI does not know your specific manager. Adjust its pushback predictions based on who you actually work for.
For managers: an AI-augmented onboarding that new hires actually appreciate.
THE STEPS

1. [AI] Ask AI to draft a 30 / 60 / 90-day plan for the specific role.
2. [YOU] Customize based on your actual team, priorities, and the specific person.
3. [YOU] In week 1, ask the new hire the same 4 questions you'd ask any team member (what's working, what isn't, what does success look like, what have you been reluctant to say).
4. [AI] Draft a personalized onboarding communication kit — who to meet in the first two weeks, what to read, what to ship first.
5. [YOU] Adjust based on the person's actual background. Send. Meet weekly.
6. [AI] At day 60, ask AI to generate reflection questions for the new hire — what should they be noticing about their fit and progress?
7. [YOU] Have the day-60 conversation. Adjust the plan honestly.
WATCH OUT FOR
• New hires notice generic onboarding. Do the customization work.
A quarterly financial reflection that most people never do.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Export your last 3 months of transactions.
2. [AI] Ask AI to categorize by fixed / variable / discretionary. Do NOT paste account numbers or sensitive identifiers.
3. [YOU] Verify the categorization is broadly right.
4. [AI] Ask AI to identify: (a) the top 3 categories of variable spending, (b) any subscription that looks recurring but rarely used, (c) any spike or unusual pattern.
5. [YOU] Review. Cancel unused subscriptions. Note the patterns you'd like to change.
6. [AI] Ask AI to help draft a revised monthly allocation given your goals.
7. [YOU] Adjust. Do the quarterly review again in 3 months. Compare.
WATCH OUT FOR

• Never send account numbers, full statements with identifiers, or SSN-like data to AI. Redact or summarize.
• AI does not know your local tax situation. Consult a professional for consequential financial decisions.

entries.title: Workflow 16: The Book Report to Yourself

blocks.text: After reading anything worth reading — a book, a paper, a long article — a workflow that turns reading into durable knowledge.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Immediately after finishing, write down: the central argument, the 5 secondary ideas, the 2 places you disagree or are unsure.
2. [AI] Feed AI your summary. Ask: (1) does this capture the book's argument fairly? (2) what important idea am I missing? (3) what would a critic of this book say?
3. [YOU] Revise your notes.
4. [AI] Ask AI for the two most credible sources that push back on the book's argument. Add them to your future-reading list.
5. [YOU] File the notes where you can find them in a year.
WATCH OUT FOR
• AI's book summaries can be shallow or wrong. Your actual reading is the ground truth.

entries.title: Workflow 17: A Difficult Feedback Session — Both Directions

blocks.text: For giving feedback well, and for receiving it.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] For giving: outline what you want to say using SBI-I structure.
2. [AI] Ask AI to critique: is this feedback specific? Does it stay on behavior? Is the underlying respect visible?
3. [YOU] Revise. Deliver in private. LMR after.
4. [YOU] For receiving: after the feedback session, write down what was said verbatim as best you can.
5. [AI] Ask AI to help you sort: which parts are likely fair, which parts are the giver's own issue, which parts are worth acting on.
6. [YOU] Decide what to change. Tell the person what you changed.
WATCH OUT FOR
• AI's sorting is a starting point, not a verdict. Your judgment about the giver's intent is more reliable than AI's guess.
For anything you'll deliver live to a real audience.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Write the FIRST DRAFT yourself. Every sentence in your voice. Bad first drafts are fine.
2. [AI] Ask AI to identify the strongest and weakest 30 seconds.
3. [YOU] Rewrite the weakest 30 seconds until it matches the strongest.
4. [AI] Ask AI to predict the 3 most likely audience questions.
5. [YOU] Prepare specific answers. Rehearse.
6. [YOU] Do a full run-through out loud, timed. Cut 10% if long.
7. [AI] Have AI critique the run-through — where does energy dip, where is the argument fuzzy, where would a listener zone out?
8. [YOU] Final pass. Deliver.
WATCH OUT FOR
• AI cannot hear you actually delivering. Record yourself and listen. That's the honest feedback.
When something has gone badly wrong at work — a public failure, an outage, a customer meltdown.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] Get calm. Level 1. Long exhale. Move if you need to.
2. [YOU] Write down what you actually know vs. what you assume.
3. [AI] Given the facts, ask AI: what are the top 3 most likely causes? What are the top 3 immediate actions? What am I likely to miss under pressure?
4. [YOU] Verify AI's suggestions against your specific context. Pick your actions.
5. [AI] Draft the initial communication to stakeholders in your voice. Include: what happened, what we're doing, when we'll update again.
6. [YOU] Send. Do the work. Update on schedule.
7. [YOU] After the crisis: write up what happened, what worked, what didn't. Share honestly.
WATCH OUT FOR

• In a real emergency, do not ask AI as your first move. Ask humans with authority to act.
• AI does not know your regulatory / legal / PR context. Loop in the specialists before external communication.
Once a year, a full workflow to look at the year honestly and set the next one deliberately.
THE STEPS

1. [YOU] List all the major moves of the year — projects, decisions, relationships, learning, health, finances.
2. [YOU] For each, note: was it my choice, or drift?
3. [AI] Feed AI the year's summary. Ask: what patterns do you see? What does this year say about how I actually operate?
4. [YOU] Sit with the reflection. Answer the 10-year audit questions (Level 8.6).
5. [AI] Ask AI to help you draft 3-5 goals for next year — not New-Year-resolution style, but specific and measurable.
6. [YOU] Choose the ONE goal that would matter most. Design the first 30 days of work on it.
7. [YOU] File everything. Look at it a year from now.
WATCH OUT FOR

• Yearly reflection often produces performative goals. Choose fewer, meaningful ones.
• AI's suggested goals can be generic. Your version must be specific to your life.
REMEMBER THIS
*“A prompt is a moment. A workflow is a practice.”*
